# Combined QED × QCD Resummation for Precision LHC Physics

## Overview and Motivation

Precision physics at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) increasingly demands theoretical predictions that account for both electromagnetic (QED) and strong (QCD) interaction effects with high accuracy. As experimental measurements achieve ever-greater precision, theoretical calculations must correspondingly improve to match this level of exactness. This paper addresses a critical gap in current theoretical methodology by presenting a comprehensive framework for the combined resummation of QED and QCD effects, recognizing that these two sectors of the Standard Model cannot be treated in isolation when aiming for percent-level or better precision in collider observables.

## The Theoretical Framework

The core contribution of this work is the development of a formalism that consistently combines QED × QCD resummation. Resummation techniques are essential tools in perturbative calculations, allowing theorists to account for large logarithmic contributions that arise from soft and collinear emissions to all orders in the coupling constants. While QCD resummation has been extensively studied and applied due to the dominance of strong interaction effects at hadron colliders, the inclusion of QED effects—arising from photon emission and electroweak corrections—introduces additional complexity that requires careful theoretical treatment when both effects must be resummed simultaneously.

The framework presented here is specifically engineered to handle the interplay between these two sectors, ensuring that the resummed results properly capture the physics of overlapping soft and collinear regions where both QED and QCD emissions can become important. This combined approach is essential because naive superposition of separately resummed QED and QCD calculations can lead to double-counting or missing contributions, particularly in regions of phase space where both types of radiation are simultaneously enhanced.

## Interface with Parton Shower Matching

A particularly important aspect of this study is its detailed examination of how the combined QED × QCD resummation framework interacts with matrix element and parton shower matching procedures. Modern LHC phenomenology relies heavily on Monte Carlo event generators that combine fixed-order matrix element calculations with parton shower algorithms to produce realistic simulated events. The matching between these two components must be handled carefully to avoid double-counting of radiative effects and to ensure that the logarithmic accuracy achieved in the resummation is preserved when interfaced with shower algorithms.

By explicitly considering this matching procedure, the authors ensure that their theoretical framework is not merely an abstract construction but is directly applicable to the practical tools used by experimentalists and theorists alike in generating predictions for LHC observables. This consideration of shower/matrix element matching represents a crucial bridge between formal resummation theory and the practical simulation tools that underpin modern collider phenomenology.

## Application to Precision LHC Physics

The framework is explicitly designed with LHC precision physics applications in mind, underscoring its practical relevance to ongoing and future experimental programs. As the LHC experiments continue to refine measurements of fundamental parameters—including the W boson mass, electroweak mixing angle, and various coupling constants—the theoretical uncertainty budget must be correspondingly reduced. Combined QED × QCD effects are known to be particularly important for observables where photon radiation from charged leptons or quarks can significantly impact the reconstructed kinematics of the process, making this framework valuable for reducing systematic theoretical uncertainties in precision measurements.

## Validation Through Single Heavy Gauge Boson Production

To demonstrate the practical utility and validity of their theoretical framework, the authors employ single heavy gauge boson production (such as W or Z boson production) as an illustrative case study. This process serves as an ideal testing ground for several reasons: it is one of the most precisely measured processes at the LHC, it involves both QCD effects from the strongly-interacting initial state and QED effects from the electroweak final state (particularly relevant for leptonic decay channels), and it has substantial phenomenological importance for extracting fundamental Standard Model parameters.

By applying their combined resummation framework to this concrete physical process, the authors are able to explicitly demonstrate how QED and QCD logarithms interplay in a realistic scenario, validate the consistency of their theoretical approach against known limits and existing calculations, and provide a template calculation that can inform future applications to other LHC processes of interest.

## Significance and Outlook

This work represents an important step toward achieving the level of theoretical precision required to fully exploit the wealth of data being collected at the LHC. By properly combining QED and QCD resummation in a unified theoretical framework—while simultaneously addressing the practical challenges of shower/matrix element matching—the authors provide both conceptual clarity and practical tools for the precision physics program at the LHC. The application to single heavy gauge boson production serves not only as validation but also as a template that can guide extensions to other processes where combined electroweak and strong interaction effects play a significant role in achieving the theoretical precision demanded by current and future experimental measurements.

# QED×QCD Resummation and Parton Shower/Matrix Element Matching for Precision LHC Physics

## Introduction

The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has ushered in an era of precision physics, where theoretical predictions must match the extraordinary experimental accuracy achieved in measurements of Standard Model processes and searches for new physics. Among the most fundamental processes studied at hadron colliders is the production of single heavy gauge bosons (W and Z), which serves not only as a benchmark for testing the Standard Model but also as a crucial calibration tool for luminosity measurements, parton distribution function extraction, and precision electroweak parameter determination, including the W boson mass.

Achieving the required theoretical precision for these processes demands a sophisticated treatment of higher-order corrections from both the strong (QCD) and electromagnetic (QED) interactions. While QCD corrections have traditionally dominated theoretical uncertainty budgets, the increasing precision goals at the LHC—particularly for W mass measurements—necessitate careful inclusion of QED effects and their proper interplay with QCD dynamics. This paper presents a theoretical framework for combined QED×QCD resummation that addresses this need, along with strategies for matching this resummed calculation to parton shower Monte Carlo generators and fixed-order matrix element calculations.

## Theoretical Framework

### QED×QCD Resummation Formalism

The resummation approach developed here builds upon established techniques in QCD resummation theory while extending them to consistently incorporate QED radiative effects. Standard QCD resummation methods, such as those based on the Collins-Soper-Sterman formalism, have long been used to resum large logarithms arising from soft and collinear gluon emission, particularly important in transverse momentum and threshold resummation for processes like Drell-Yan production. However, single heavy gauge boson production also receives significant electromagnetic radiative corrections since these bosons carry electric charge (in the case of W) or couple to charged leptons in the final state.

Our framework generalizes the resummation formalism to treat QED and QCD emissions on equal footing, recognizing that both types of radiation can generate large logarithmic contributions that must be resummed to all orders in perturbation theory. This involves:

1. **Extending the evolution equations**: The renormalization group equations governing the resummation are extended to include both QCD and QED anomalous dimensions, capturing the mixed QED×QCD contributions that arise starting at specific orders in the combined coupling expansion.

2. **Coherent treatment of soft/collinear radiation**: We develop a unified treatment of soft and collinear photon and gluon emissions, ensuring proper factorization of the cross section into hard, soft, and collinear functions that consistently incorporate both interaction types.

3. **Matching to fixed-order calculations**: The resummed expressions are matched to fixed-order QED and QCD calculations to ensure accurate predictions across the entire kinematic range, from the resummation-dominated region to the region where fixed-order perturbation theory is most reliable.

### Numerical Implementation and Structure

The combined resummation formalism requires careful bookkeeping of the counting scheme for logarithmic accuracy. We work at a level of precision that captures the dominant logarithmic structures from both QCD and QED radiation, specifying the accuracy achieved (e.g., next-to-leading logarithmic or higher) for each type of radiation and their interference.

## Matching to Parton Showers and Matrix Elements

A central theoretical and practical challenge addressed in this paper concerns the consistent matching of the QED×QCD resummed calculation to parton shower Monte Carlo (PS) generators and fixed-order matrix element (ME) calculations, which are essential tools for realistic experimental simulations at the LHC.

### Parton Shower Matching

Modern parton shower algorithms, whether based on QCD-only evolution or including QED radiation (as in programs like PHOTOS, HERWIG, or PYTHIA with QED shower extensions), provide fully differential predictions for exclusive final states but typically capture only leading logarithmic accuracy. Matching our resummed calculation to parton showers requires:

- Identifying the logarithmic structure already captured by the shower algorithm to avoid double-counting
- Developing subtraction schemes that remove the logarithms already present in the shower approximation while retaining the higher-logarithmic-accuracy resummation
- Ensuring smooth interpolation between the resummation-dominated soft/collinear region and the hard emission region governed by fixed-order matrix elements

### Matrix Element Matching

For observables sensitive to hard, well-separated emissions, matching to fixed-order matrix elements is essential. We present a matching prescription that combines the resummed QED×QCD calculation with next-to-leading order (NLO) QCD and QED matrix elements, following strategies analogous to those developed for pure QCD resummation (such as the MC@NLO or POWHEG matching schemes), but extended to consistently treat the additional QED radiation and its interference with QCD effects.

## Application to Single Heavy Gauge Boson Production

We illustrate the practical implementation and phenomenological impact of this combined resummation and matching framework using single W and Z boson production at hadron colliders as a testing ground. This process is particularly well-suited as an illustrative case for several reasons:

1. **Phenomenological importance**: W and Z production are benchmark Standard Model processes at the LHC, with the W mass measurement representing one of the most demanding precision tests requiring exquisite theoretical control over QED and QCD radiative effects.

2. **Clean theoretical laboratory**: The relatively simple partonic structure of single boson production (compared to more complex multi-particle final states) allows for a clear demonstration of the resummation formalism without excessive theoretical complications.

3. **Existing precision QCD tools**: The extensive existing literature on QCD resummation for Drell-Yan-like processes provides a solid foundation upon which to build and validate our extended QED×QCD framework.

We present numerical results for key observables such as the transverse momentum distribution of the gauge boson and its decay leptons, angular distributions of the charged lepton, and the reconstructed W mass observables, demonstrating the quantitative impact of the combined QED×QCD resummation compared to QCD-only or naive QED+QCD additive approaches.

## Phenomenological Impact and Precision Considerations

The results demonstrate that the interplay between QED and QCD radiative corrections cannot generally be treated as a simple additive combination of separate QED and QCD effects. Mixed logarithmic contributions and the interference between soft photon and soft gluon emission can produce non-trivial effects on differential distributions, particularly in kinematic regions sensitive to soft and collinear radiation. These effects are especially relevant for:

- Precision extraction of the W boson mass, where lepton momentum and missing transverse energy distributions are highly sensitive to QED final-state radiation
- Determination of parton distribution functions from Drell-Yan data, where QED corrections can shift the extracted PDF values at a level comparable to current experimental uncertainties
- Any precision electroweak measurement relying on accurate theoretical modeling of gauge boson production and decay

## Conclusion

This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for combined QED×QCD resummation and its matching to parton shower and matrix element calculations, addressing an essential precision frontier in LHC physics. By using single heavy gauge boson production as an illustrative and phenomenologically critical test case, we demonstrate the practical implementation of this formalism and quantify its impact on key observables.

The tools developed here represent an important step toward the theoretical precision required for current and future LHC measurements, particularly as the experimental precision on electroweak observables continues to improve with increased integrated luminosity. The combined QED×QCD resummation and matching framework presented in this work provides essential theoretical infrastructure for the broader LHC precision physics program, enabling more accurate interpretation of experimental data and more reliable extraction of fundamental Standard Model parameters. Future extensions of this framework to other processes and further refinements in matching accuracy will continue to enhance the precision toolkit available for LHC physics analyses.

# Quantum Field Theories and the Large Hadron Collider

Modern particle physics rests on two pillars of quantum field theory: Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) and Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). Both are essential to understanding the results produced by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the world's most powerful particle accelerator.

## Quantum Electrodynamics (QED)

QED is the quantum field theory describing the electromagnetic interaction between charged particles, mediated by photons. Developed in the 1940s by physicists such as Richard Feynman, Julian Schwinger, and Sin-Itiro Tomonaga, QED is remarkable for its extraordinary precision. Predictions like the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron agree with experimental measurements to more than ten decimal places, making QED one of the most rigorously tested theories in all of science.

## Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD)

QCD describes the strong nuclear force, which binds quarks and gluons together to form protons, neutrons, and other hadrons. Unlike QED, QCD exhibits a property called *color confinement*, meaning quarks and gluons cannot be isolated and are always found bound within composite particles. QCD also displays *asymptotic freedom* — at very high energies, the strong force becomes weaker, allowing quarks to behave almost like free particles. This property is crucial for calculations in high-energy collisions, such as those occurring at the LHC.

## The Large Hadron Collider (LHC)

Located at CERN near Geneva, Switzerland, the LHC is a 27-kilometer circular accelerator that collides protons (and sometimes heavy ions) at nearly the speed of light. Since protons are composite particles made of quarks and gluons, understanding LHC collisions requires QCD to model the complex interactions and jet formations that occur. Meanwhile, QED plays a role in describing electromagnetic processes and interactions involving photons and charged leptons produced in these collisions.

The LHC's most celebrated achievement was the 2012 discovery of the Higgs boson, confirming the mechanism by which fundamental particles acquire mass. This discovery relied heavily on precise theoretical predictions combining both QED and QCD within the Standard Model of particle physics.

## Conclusion

QED and QCD together form the theoretical backbone needed to interpret the vast amounts of data generated by the LHC. Their combined framework, part of the Standard Model, has enabled physicists to test fundamental theories with remarkable accuracy and continues to guide the search for new physics beyond our current understanding.

# Abstract

We present a formalism for combining QED and QCD resummation to achieve precision predictions for single heavy gauge boson production at the LHC, addressing the interplay between electroweak and strong-interaction corrections in a unified framework. Building on transverse-momentum resummation techniques, we extend the standard QCD treatment to consistently incorporate final-state photon radiation and mixed QCD⊗QED effects at next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy, matched to fixed-order perturbative results at next-to-leading order in both couplings. Particular attention is devoted to the treatment of collinear photon emission from initial-state quarks, mass singularities associated with the lepton pair invariant mass, and the proper factorization of QED and QCD radiation in the resummed exponent, including their mixed contributions arising from simultaneous soft and collinear gluon and photon emission.

We demonstrate how this combined resummation framework can be matched consistently onto parton-shower Monte Carlo generators, providing a bridge between resummed analytic calculations and the fully differential, exclusive final states required for realistic experimental analyses. Using the Drell-Yan process $pp \to Z/\gamma^* \to \ell^+\ell^-$ (and the charged-current analogue $pp \to W \to \ell\nu$) as a benchmark, we quantify the impact of QED resummation and its interplay with QCD dynamics on key observables, including the transverse momentum and rapidity distributions of the gauge boson and the reconstructed invariant/transverse mass spectra relevant for precision measurements of the $W$ boson mass and the weak mixing angle. We show that the combined treatment yields percent-level shifts in these distributions relative to predictions where QCD and QED effects are treated independently or where QED corrections are included only at fixed order, with the size of these effects being commensurate with the precision goals of current and future LHC measurements.

Our results establish that a consistent combined QCD+QED resummation, properly matched to parton showers, is essential for controlling theoretical uncertainties in precision electroweak measurements at the LHC, and we provide a practical framework for its implementation in general-purpose Monte Carlo tools used by the experimental collaborations.

# Unified Framework for Electroweak-QCD Resummation with Shower/ME Matching

## Overview

This theoretical framework addresses a central challenge in precision predictions for hadron collider observables: consistently combining higher-order electroweak (EW) corrections with QCD resummation, while maintaining compatibility with parton shower Monte Carlo (PSMC) matching schemes. The approach is particularly relevant for benchmark processes such as **Drell-Yan W/Z production**, where percent-level precision is now required to match experimental accuracy at the LHC.

## Key Theoretical Components

**1. Joint QCD⊗EW Resummation**

The framework treats large logarithms from both QCD (soft/collinear gluon emission) and electroweak (Sudakov EW logs from soft/collinear W, Z, γ emission at high energy) sectors on equal footing. Using factorization theorems rooted in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET) or analogous QCD resummation formalisms, the cross section is organized as:

$$
d\sigma = d\sigma_{\rm QCD-res} \times \left[1 + \Delta_{\rm EW}(\alpha_s, \alpha)\right] + \text{mixed } \alpha_s\alpha \text{ terms}
$$

Mixed QCD×EW logarithms (arising from simultaneous soft gluon and soft photon/weak boson emission) require careful treatment to avoid double-counting, typically handled via a factorized ansatz separating collinear PDF evolution (QCD+QED), soft-wide-angle radiation, and hard matching coefficients.

**2. Matching to Parton Showers**

To retain full kinematic and multiplicity information beyond fixed-order/resummed inclusive predictions, the resummed calculation is matched to a parton shower using **MC@NLO** or **POWHEG**-type methods extended to include:
- QED/EW radiation via QED-enabled showers (e.g., PHOTOS-like or full EW shower algorithms)
- Consistent subtraction of double-counted logarithms between analytic resummation and shower resummation
- Preservation of NLO EW accuracy in the hard matrix element while showers generate realistic multi-particle final states

**3. Matched Observable Structure**

For transverse momentum spectra of the W/Z boson, the differential cross section takes a schematic matched form:

$$
\frac{d\sigma}{dp_T} = \frac{d\sigma^{\rm resum}_{\rm QCD+EW}}{dp_T}\Big|_{p_T\to 0} + \frac{d\sigma^{\rm fixed-order}}{dp_T}\Big|_{p_T\sim M_W} - \text{overlap}
$$

with EW Sudakov effects becoming numerically significant (several percent) in the high-$p_T$ tail, while QCD resummation dominates the low-$p_T$ Sudakov shoulder.

## Application: W/Z Production Case Study

For **Z→ℓℓ** and **W→ℓν** production:
- QCD resummation (NNLL or higher) governs the transverse momentum and rapidity distributions at low-to-moderate $p_T$
- EW corrections modify the high-$p_T$ tail through Sudakov logarithms $\sim \alpha \ln^2(M_W^2/\hat s)$, relevant for precision $M_W$ extraction
- Multi-photon final-state radiation (FSR) is resummed via YFS-type exponentiation, matched to shower-generated QED radiation
- The interplay directly impacts extraction of $\sin^2\theta_W$, $M_W$, and PDF-sensitive observables, requiring the combined treatment for sub-percent theoretical uncertainty

## Significance

This unified framework provides the theoretical backbone for modern precision tools (e.g., **MATRIX+RadISH**, **POWHEG-EW**, or dedicated **SCET-based generators**), enabling percent-level predictions essential for LHC precision electroweak measurements and BSM sensitivity studies where both large logarithmic QCD effects and genuine EW Sudakov behavior must be simultaneously controlled.

# Abstract

We present a theoretical framework combining QED×QCD resummation with matrix element and parton shower (MC@NLO/POWHEG-type) matching for precision predictions of single heavy gauge boson (W/Z) production at the LHC. The formalism, based on the YFS (Yennie-Frautschi-Suura) exponentiation extended to include coherent QCD effects alongside multiple soft/collinear photon radiation, allows for a consistent treatment of higher-order electroweak and QCD corrections without double-counting. We discuss the implementation of this approach within a Monte Carlo event generator, emphasizing the systematic matching between fixed-order NLO QCD/EW matrix elements and all-orders resummed parton showers. Particular attention is given to the numerical impact of QED×QCD interference effects on key observables, including the transverse momentum and rapidity distributions of the W/Z bosons and their decay leptons, as well as the reconstructed boson mass line-shape relevant for precision electroweak measurements such as the W mass determination. We quantify the size of mixed QED-QCD corrections relative to pure QCD or pure QED contributions and assess the associated theoretical uncertainties from scale variations and matching scheme dependence. Comparisons with available fixed-order NNLO QCD+NLO EW predictions and public parton shower tools illustrate the level of agreement and highlight regions of phase space where resummation effects are most significant. These results underscore the necessity of combined QED×QCD resummation for achieving the sub-percent theoretical precision required by current and future LHC electroweak precision programs, particularly for the W boson mass and effective weak mixing angle extractions.

# Abstract

Precision phenomenology at the LHC increasingly demands theoretical predictions that match the exquisite statistical power of the data. For processes such as single vector boson (W/Z) production, percent-level accuracy requires the simultaneous control of QCD and QED radiative effects, since both soft and collinear emissions from partons and leptons contribute at comparable orders once electroweak corrections are included. This talk addresses the challenge of consistently combining QCD and QED resummation within a unified framework, focusing on transverse-momentum and threshold-sensitive observables where large logarithms from both sectors must be resummed to all orders without double-counting or spurious mixed-order artifacts.

I will discuss the structure of joint QCD⊗QED resummation, highlighting the role of factorization in disentangling universal soft/collinear radiation from process-dependent hard functions, and the subtleties introduced by final-state photon radiation and its interplay with parton distribution functions evolved under QED-extended DGLAP equations. Particular attention is given to matching these resummed predictions onto fixed-order NNLO QCD and NLO EW calculations, ensuring a well-defined counting scheme that avoids overlapping logarithmic contributions.

A central theme of the talk is the consistency between resummed/fixed-order predictions and parton-shower Monte Carlo generators, which implement analogous QCD and QED radiation through very different organizing principles. I will examine how shower algorithms accommodate higher-order splitting functions, coherence effects, and photon radiation off charged leptons, and how their logarithmic accuracy can be benchmarked against analytic resummation. Using single vector boson production as a case study, I will present comparisons of transverse-momentum spectra and lepton observables sensitive to the W mass and PDF determinations, illustrating both the current level of agreement across frameworks and residual sources of theoretical uncertainty. I will conclude with an outlook on the requirements for achieving a fully consistent QCD+QED description at the precision demanded by future LHC measurements.

The approach systematically merges higher-order perturbative QCD corrections (resummed to account for soft and collinear gluon emissions) with QED corrections (accounting for photon radiation effects), while ensuring consistency with fixed-order matrix element calculations to avoid double-counting of emissions in the overlapping regions.

The method is validated through its application to heavy gauge boson production (such as W and Z bosons) at hadron colliders, a process sensitive to both QCD dynamics from the initial-state partons and QED effects from final-state charged lepton radiation. By demonstrating the combined resummation and matching procedure in this context, the study shows improved theoretical accuracy in describing kinematic distributions—such as transverse momentum and invariant mass spectra—that are crucial for precision electroweak measurements, including the determination of the W boson mass. This unified approach provides a robust tool for interpreting collider data with reduced theoretical uncertainties stemming from missing higher-order QCD and QED effects.
